title: A certified core beyond the weighted-jet cone
analyticalQuestion: Can an explicit four-real-dimensional 1:2:3 coefficient core start beyond Q2<=1/2, cross that sufficient boundary under heat decay, and retain a uniform two-critical-point shape contract?
supportedTakeaway: The polydisc |z2-3/20|<=1/100, |z3|<=1/1000 starts at Q2>=14/25>1/2. Every heat path crosses Q2=1/2 exactly once while retaining two critical points. On 0<=y<=1 the physical shape contract is (r,C0,C1)=(pi/48,144,240). The real slice and heat curves shown are direct samples of exact formulas.
analyticClaims: The full complex polydisc has nonempty interior in four real dimensions and is uniformly outside the old Q2<=1/2 sufficient cone at y=0.
The center 1:2 slope factor is at least 2/5; complex perturbations have first and second derivative budgets 23/1000 and 49/1000.
Every normalized heat profile has exactly two critical points in fixed pi/48 boxes and the conservative local normalized slope comparison (1/4)d<|F'|<(5/3)d.
For W=e^{-y}F on 0<=y<=1, the conservative shape constants are C0=144 and C1=240.
The real 1:2:3 slice has endpoint walls and the closed internal arc a=-2x/(1+4x^2), b=1/[3(1+4x^2)] for -1<=x<=1.
Q2(y)=4|z2|e^{-3y}+9|z3|e^{-8y} decreases strictly, begins above 1/2, and is below 20489/256000 at y=1.
finiteDiagnostics: Every plotted curve is a direct sample of an exact analytic formula.
Sampling cannot replace the continuous proof.
No PDE evolution, regression, exponent fit, or numerical root classification is run.
The certificate files gate lineage and are not plotted as mathematical evidence.
Temporary or unsealed certificate crosschecks are rejected.
The complete four-dimensional caustic decomposition is not claimed.

panelClaims.A: The real coefficient slice shows the exact endpoint walls, the true internal unit-circle arc, the old Q2 diamond, and the small real trace of K.
panelClaims.B: The exact heat envelopes start above Q2=1/2 and enter the old cone without a critical-point collision.
panelClaims.C: The declared local and away-gradient envelopes distinguish normalized F from the physical W contract.

Arnol'd's prior caustic and chamber topology are not claimed as new.
